But methodological discipline is required here. {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=distinctions+between+hypothesis-falsification+loops+and+foundational+meta-reasoning+in+autonomous+agents&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6759126\", \"title\": [\"An Engineering Framework for Self-Correcting Autonomous AI Agents: Mitigating Hallucinations and Reasoning Loops in Autonomous Engineering Workflows\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This paper presents TRACE (Trajectory Reliability and Correction Engine), a runtime self-correction framework for autonomous AI agents in engineering workflows. TRACE targets a reliability gap in multi-step tool-using agents, where unsupported claims, contradictions, repetitive loops, and tool-use anomalies can propagate across long execution trajectories. Existing self-correction methods typically rely on post-hoc reflection or a single intervention mechanism, but do not integrate continuous runtime monitoring, failure attribution, and adaptive recovery in one control layer. TRACE wraps a standard ReAct-style agent with four modules: a Trajectory Monitor, a Failure Attribution module, a Recovery Controller, and an Audit Layer for structured trace logging. We evaluate TRACE on a simulated enterprise incident-triage benchmark of 50 tasks with injected hallucination- and loop-inducing conditions across four difficulty levels. TRACE achieves 76.0% task success versus 68.0% for a self-reflection baseline and 62.0% for vanilla ReAct, while reducing hallucination incidence from 19.4% to 9.6% and loop frequency from 12.1% to 4.8%. The framework is intended for reliable, auditable autonomous execution in engineering environments.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6759126\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6956178\", \"title\": [\"Cognitive Internet Layer (CIL): The Foundational Trust and Reasoning Infrastructure for Autonomous Intelligence Systems\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The current internet architecture was fundamentally designed for deterministic data packet transport and applicationlevel request-response interactions, not for the semantic exchange, verification, governance, and replay of autonomous machine reasoning. {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=AI+systems+reflexive+self-correction+foundational+epistemic+assumptions&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"On qualitizing revisited.\", \"abstract\": \"The original definition of qualitizing-the conversion of quantitative data into qualitative form-has made an important contribution to mixed methods research but presented a reductionist view that overlooked its interpretive and integrative dimensions. Building on Onwuegbuzie and Leech's (2019) meta-framework, the present article reconceptualizes qualitizing as a recursive, meaning-centered, and meta-integrative process grounded in Critical Dialectical Pluralism (CDP) 2.0. Through this metaphilosophical lens, qualitizing is reframed not as a mechanical act of data conversion but as a meta-transformative process of interpretive synthesis that unites quantitative precision with qualitative depth across research traditions. To operationalize this expanded understanding, the article introduces a 43-profile Narrative Profiling Taxonomy-a theoretically grounded yet empirically generative framework for transforming quantitative, qualitative, or mixed data into interpretive narratives that embody full integration (in a representational sense). These profiles illustrate how numerical structures can be humanized through narrative representation, allowing meta-inferences that transcend analytic boundaries. Although extensive, the taxonomy is not presented as exhaustive but as an evolving representation of the current state of qualitizing's methodological and epistemological potential. It introduces arts-based extensions highlighting the analytic, affective, and creative dimensions of integration. In re-envisioning qualitizing as a multidimensional system of meaning-making, On Qualitizing Revisited advances the integrative ideal of Onwuegbuzie and Hitchcock's (2019) 1 + 1 = 1 integration approach, wherein data transformation becomes an act of synthesis rather than conversion.
